Cell 27 would therefore build 15-epoch files, and cell 30's score filter would yield 533 trials, not the 48 x 12 = 576 constant-12 blocks shown in cell 31 ((12, 3) events) and printed in cell 32 (class counts 144/96/112/144/80). The recorded label vectors cannot be produced by the committed annotation/score tables, so scout-challenge's claim that 'the 12-id vectors are valid subsequences of the 15-entry session lists' is not a valid consistency proof: each of the two recorded patterns is a subsequence of one session list, but the per-session filter does not produce a constant 12 per file and the class counts differ. This strengthens the provenance break rather than refuting it.

Subject-level leakage is not provable from the repository: cells 12 (KeyboardInterrupt), 25 and 29 (%%capture) print no file names or listing order, so neither the mapping of the 48 blocks to subjects nor a subject-major listdir order can be established. What is provable is session-level: 460 mod 12 = 4, so the 12-epoch block at indices 456-467 straddles the train/val boundary and at least one recording session contributes to both partitions. The claims 'group 12 straddles train and val' and 'groups 12..15 lie entirely inside val' assume an unshown ordering.

The scouts' statistics re-check exactly: exact binomial 28/115 vs 0.20 gives p = 0.2441; vs 29/115 gives p = 0.9146; Wilson 95% CI [17.42%, 32.94%]. These support 'null-compatible / indistinguishable from a constant predictor', not 'no learning proven', and the article's own reported numbers were not read or compared, so no notebook-vs-article claim was made. Nothing in this review was executed; the SEED-V data is absent.
